items.title: 한울반도체, 20억원 유상증자 모집에 104억원 청약 흥행

items.snippet: 인천 강화도에서 북한에서 유실된 것으로 추정되는 지뢰가 또 발견됐다.19일 강화군에 따르면 이날 오전 11시13분께 강화군 볼음도 조갯골 해안 인근에서 해병대2사단이 해안수색 정찰 중 반보병지뢰 1개를 발견했다.군 당국은 폭발물처리반(EOD)를 투입해 이날 오후 1시26분께 현장에서 지뢰를 폭파 처리했다. 이 과정에서 인적·물적 피해는 발생하지 않았다.강화군은 해당 지뢰가 지난 여름철 호우에 북한에서 유실돼 떠내려온 것으로 추정하고 있다.이날 처리된 지뢰를 포함해 강화도에서는 이달에만 북한이 매설했다가 유실된 것으로 추정되는 지뢰가 4번째 발견됐다.지난 8일 서도면 주문도 대빈창해수욕장 인근에서 반보병지뢰 1개, 10일께는 주문도 응구지 해안와 불은면 오두돈대 인근 해상에서 반보명지뢰 1개와 목함지뢰 1개가 각각 발견됐다.[인천=뉴시스]

items.snippet: 지난 16일 경기 부천의 금속 공장 화재 현장에서 진화 작업을 하다 중태에 빠진 김진석(44) 소방위가 다음 날 새벽 숨졌다. 김 소방위는 퇴근을 20여 분 앞두고 현장에 가장 먼저 출동했다. 내년 초등학교 입학을 앞둔 여섯 살 딸을 둔 가장이었다. 순천향대 부천병원 장례식장에 마련된 빈소에는 시민과 동료 소방관들의 추모 발길이 이어졌다. 이재명 대통령은 17일 빈소를 찾아 유족을 위로했다. 정부는 김 소방위를 소방장에서 소방위로 1계급 특진시키고 옥조근정훈장을 추서했다.

items.title: 무늬만 국가직 전환… 지역마다 소방관 처우·안전 장비 큰 격차
items.snippet: 문재인 정부는 2020년 대부분 지방직이던 소방공무원을 국가직으로 전환했다. 방수 장갑이 없어 면장갑을 끼고 불을 끄거나 장비를 사비로 구입해 쓰는 현실이 알려진 뒤였다. 소방관을 보호해야 할 방화복이 불에 녹아내린 사례도 있었다. 지방자치단체의 재정 형편에 따른 격차를 없애자는 취지였다.

items.snippet: 재벌 회장 아들이 파티장에서 직원 아내를 유혹한다. 이를 본 직원은 회장 아들의 뺨을 후려친다. 주변 사람들이 술렁이자 이 직원은 갑자기 “나도 다른 재벌 그룹 회장”이라고 정체를 밝히며, 아내를 희롱한 재벌 일가를 향해 복수를 선언한다. 유튜브에 올라온 1분짜리 중국 ‘숏폼 드라마’다. 그런데 이 숏폼 드라마 화면 속 배우들은 실존 인물이 아니다. 모두 인공지능(AI)이 만들어낸 가상 인물이다. 이들이 연기하는 대본도 AI가 썼다.

items.title: ‘DMZ 지뢰’ 李 고발 사건 놓고… 서로 미루는 수사기관들
items.snippet: 한 시민단체가 비무장지대(DMZ) 지뢰 폭발과 관련해 이재명 대통령을 일반이적 혐의 등으로 고발한 사건을 두고, 경찰이 예정돼 있던 고발인 조사를 미루려다가 시민단체의 항의를 받고 예정대로 진행한 것으로 18일 확인됐다. 시민단체 관계자는 본지에 “경찰은 사건을 중대범죄수사청(중수청)이나 고위공직자범죄수사처(공수처)에 넘기려고 하고, 다른 수사기관들은 서로 안 맡으려는 분위기 같다”며 “12·3 비상계엄 당시 윤석열 전 대통령을 수사할 때 검찰과 경찰, 공수처가 서로 달려들던 모습하고는 딴판”이라고 말했다.

items.title: 비대면 진료, 초진 약 처방은 7일치만… “고혈압·당뇨 환자들 불편”
items.snippet: 오는 12월 24일부터 비대면 진료 시 ‘초진(初診) 환자’는 원칙적으로 환자 주소지와 같은 시·도에 있는 의원급 의료기관에서만 진료를 받을 수 있을 것으로 보인다. 약도 7일 치까지만 처방받을 수 있고, 예외적으로 1회에 한해서만 최대 30일 치를 받을 수 있다. 비대면 진료를 정식 제도화하면서 촘촘한 규제를 적용해 환자들의 이용 문턱을 높였다는 지적이 나온다. 비대면 진료 플랫폼 업체들은 “사실상 비대면 진료를 하지 말라는 얘기”라며 반발하고 있다.

items.title: [신문은 선생님] [뉴스 속 신화] 불화의 여신 ‘에리스’ 등장한 뒤, 명왕성 행성 지위 잃었죠
items.snippet: 최근 캐나다 시인 앤 카슨이 2026년 노벨 문학상을 받았어요. 매년 노벨 문학상 결과가 발표되면 수상 작가의 작품이 서점에서 큰 인기를 끌곤 하죠. 그런데 카슨의 많은 작품이 주로 그리스 신화를 소재로 만들어졌다는 사실, 알고 계셨나요? 가령 ‘녹스’라는 책 제목은 그리스 신화에 등장하는 밤의 여신인 ‘닉스’의 로마식 이름입니다. 그리스 신화는 로마로 유입되면서 내용은 그대로인 채 신이나 주인공 이름만 달라졌어요. 또한 그리스 신의 로마식 이름에서 영어식 이름이 나왔으니 그리스 신의 이름은 두 개가 더 있는 셈이에요. 오늘은 신들의 이름에 대해 알아보겠습니다.

items.title: [신문은 선생님] [산 이야기] 구름바다 위 솟은 ‘설악산의 심장’… 바위들이 공룡의 등처럼 보인대요
items.snippet: 강원도 속초와 양양, 인제, 고성에 걸쳐 우뚝 솟은 설악산의 ‘공룡능선’은 ‘설악산의 심장’으로 불립니다. 국립공원공단이 국립공원의 아름다운 풍경 100선을 꼽으며 공룡능선을 가장 빼어난 곳으로 선정했을 정도로 압도적인 절경을 자랑합니다. ‘공룡능선’은 인제와 속초 사이 고개인 마등령에서 시작해 신선대까지 5㎞ 이어진 능선이에요. 여기엔 뾰족한 바위들이 촘촘하게 솟아 있습니다. 설악산 최고봉인 대청봉(1708m)에 올라 이 능선을 내려다보면, 바위 봉우리들이 공룡의 등처럼 힘차게 솟아 있어서 ‘공룡능선’이란 이름이 붙었습니다.

items.title: 철도 깔고, 도로 다듬고… 기업과 사람이 모이는 ‘활력 도시’로
items.snippet: 지역 곳곳을 연결하는 철도와 도로망이 확충되면서 기업하기 좋은 여건이 만들어졌다. 그러자 양질의 일자리를 찾아 사람들이 몰려왔다. 대구 달성군 이야기다. 2016년 22만3585명이던 달성군 인구는 올해 6월 말 기준 26만339명으로 16%이상 늘었다. 1995년 3월 대구시 편입 당시보다는 두 배 이상으로 증가했다. 4곳이던 산업단지는 8곳으로 늘어났다. 지난 6월 지방선거를 통해 재선에 성공한 최재훈 달성군수는 초선 때부터 시민들이 오가는 대중교통 확장은 물론 기업들의 물류 여건 개선 등 교통 인프라 확충에 공을 들였다. 결국 대형 국책 사업 유치도 연이어 성공했다. 편리한 교통과 일자리 덕분에 주민도 늘고, 이들의 삶도 빛나는 선순환이 이어지고 있는 것이다.

items.title: Engineering nonrelativistic spin splitting in semiconductors by altermagnetic proximity
items.abstract: Altermagnets combine vanishing net magnetization with momentum-dependent, nonrelativistic spin splitting, offering functionalities attractive for spintronics and quantum devices. Their practical use, however, is constrained by the limited availability of materials that simultaneously possess the required altermagnetic symmetry, semiconducting electronic structure, and weak spin-orbit coupling. Here we show that these requirements can instead be separated between constituent materials through proximity engineering. We develop an analytical theory for a conventional semiconductor coupled to a gapped $d$-wave altermagnet and demonstrate that virtual tunneling transfers the altermagnetic spin splitting to the semiconductor. items.title: “땅값 반토막났는데 농지조사까지… 거래도 대출도 막혀”
items.snippet: 박영규(72)씨는 경기 여주시에서 태어나 평생 농사만 지었다. 부모에게 물려받은 땅에 농사를 지으며 조금씩 사들인 땅까지, 그가 가진 농지는 총 1만3000평이다. 박씨에게는 노후 생활비로 쓰려고 평생 모은 ‘퇴직금’이 이 땅이다. 농사를 그만두려고 마음먹은 지 한참이 됐지만, 몇 년째 땅을 못 팔고 있다. 박씨는 “평당 20만원 하던 땅인데 지금은 10만원에 내놔도 쳐다보는 사람도 없다”며 “땅값이 떨어지니까 농지를 담보로 돈을 빌리기도 어려워졌다”고 했다.

items.title: 北인공기 그려진 미사일 모형 설치… 노원구 미술축제 논란
items.snippet: 서울 노원구가 16일 개막한 공공 미술 축제에 북한 인공기가 그려진 미사일 조형물이 설치됐다. 시민들 사이에선 “시민이 오가는 공공 장소에 북한 인공기가 그려진 작품을 설치하는 게 말이 되느냐”는 비판이 나왔다. 이에 대해 노원구는 “해당 작품이 당초 계획안과 다르게 설치됐다”고 해명했다.

items.title: 미인가 국제학교들 “대안교육기관 받아달라”
items.snippet: 교육 당국의 고발 조치와 폐쇄 명령으로 문 닫을 위기에 처한 미인가 국제학교들이 법 개정을 통해 ‘대안교육기관’으로 등록하게 해달라고 국회에 요구하고 나섰다. 16일 본지 취재에 따르면, 미인가 국제학교 100여 곳은 최근 여러 국회의원실을 찾아 대안교육기관법 개정을 요청했으며, 조만간 관련 법안이 발의될 것으로 알려졌다. 교육 당국은 이들 미인가 국제학교에 불법 운영 사실을 2차례 고지했고, 시정하지 않으면 경찰에 고발·수사의뢰할 수 있다며 최후통첩한 상황이다.

items.title: 반도체 배우러, 폴리텍대 다시 가는 직장인들
items.snippet: 4년제 대학에서 영상애니메이션디자인을 전공한 김희건(27)씨는 졸업 후 게임 업계 취업을 준비하다 올해 한국폴리텍대 대구캠퍼스 그린반도체시스템과에 다시 입학했다. 최근 생성형 인공지능(AI)이 급속도로 발전하면서 디자인 분야 채용이 줄어드는 것을 보고 진로를 바꾼 것이다. AI 산업이 커질수록 반도체도 유망할 것이라는 생각이 들었다고 한다. 김씨는 “SK하이닉스에서 ‘억 소리’ 나는 성과급이 나온다는 이야기도 진로 선택에 영향을 미쳤다”고 했다.

items.title: 옹기종기 모여 ‘보랏빛 향기’
items.snippet: 16일 오전 대전 유성구 유림공원을 찾은 어린이들이 보랏빛 국화꽃 향기를 맡으며 즐거운 시간을 보내고 있다. 이곳에선 17일부터 다음 달 1일까지 대전시 대표 가을 행사인 ‘유성국화축제’가 펼쳐지며, 개막 당일에는 축하 음악회와 드론 쇼 등이 열린다.

items.title: 상대 아픈 곳 찌르고 조롱하는 말
items.snippet: 가려운 데가 있으면 손톱으로 시원하게 긁어야 하고, 기분 좋은 일이 있으면 화끈하게 카드를 긁어야 한다. 사전에 올라 있는 ‘긁다’의 첫 번째 뜻과 마지막 뜻은 이러하다. 갈퀴로 나뭇잎을 긁고 주걱으로 누룽지를 긁는 것은 순한 뜻이다. 그러나 남을 헐뜯거나 재산을 빼앗는 것, 남의 기분을 상하게 하거나 공연히 일을 키우는 것, 기관총을 마구 쏘아대는 것은 그리 좋은 뜻은 아니다. 그런데 요즘의 쓰임을 보면 ‘긁?’도 사전에 올려야 하는 것은 아닌가 하는 의문이 든다.

items.title: 위스키, 위기일까 기회일까
items.snippet: 스카치위스키가 위기라고 한다. 스코틀랜드 창고에서 숙성 중인 오크통은 약 2200만 통, 50억L가 넘는다. 영국 파이낸셜타임스(FT)는 이 가운데 팔릴 양보다 더 만들어 쌓아 둔 잉여 원액만 14억L에 달한다고 보도했다. 10년 전 4억L에도 못 미치던 양이 3.5배 이상으로 불어난 것이다. 2008년 리먼 브러더스 사태 이후 저금리로 갈 곳 잃은 돈이 위스키 같은 실물자산으로 몰렸다. 결정적 계기는 코로나19였다. ‘홈술’ 열풍 속에 오래 두고 마실 수 있는 위스키가 주목받았다. 업계가 더 많이 만들어 쌓아 둔 건 당연한 선택이었다.

items.title: 부드럽게 풀려 산뜻하게 녹아드는 맛
items.snippet: 어머니와 스시를 먹으면 꼭 아버지 이야기를 하게 된다. “너희 아빠가 그렇게 스시를 좋아했는데 나중엔 먹지도 못하고.” 아버지는 간암 진단을 받고 얼마 후에 의사에게서 ‘날것을 삼가는 게 좋겠다’는 말을 들었다. 그 이후 아버지는 날것을 먹지 않았다. 어머니도 덩달아 스시 먹을 일이 사라졌다. 평생 먹는 것을 참는 게 힘들던 아버지는 생애 마지막에는 그 어떤 음식을 가져가도 고개를 저었다. 아버지께 ‘드시라’고 애원하는 날이 찾아오리라고는 생각하지 못했다. 아버지와 달리 어머니는 먹는 데 취미가 없었다. 건강 진단을 받으면 백이면 백 “식사를 잘해야 한다”는 말을 듣는 것도 오래됐다. 회사 쉬는 날 어머니와 따로 약속을 잡는 데는, 한 끼라도 제대로 채워주고 싶은 노림수도 있었다.

items.title: 그 시절, 좋은 지도자들
items.snippet: 1985년 3월에 54세의 미하일 고르바초프가 소련 최고 지도자로 선출됐습니다. 그는 ‘새로운 사고(思考)’를 내세우며 ‘페레스트로이카’와 ‘글라스노스트’, 즉 ‘개혁’과 ‘개방’을 주창했습니다. 이른바 ‘민주주의적 공산주의’를 주장한 것입니다. 그것은 폴란드 철학자 레셰크 코와코프스키가 사용한 표현에 따르면 ‘구워진 눈덩이’와 같은 것이었습니다. 과연 고르바초프가 눈덩이를 구울 수 있을까? 큰 의문이었습니다. 그는 비정통적인 방식의 협상 제안과 매력적인 공격으로 서방 측을 부드럽게 압박했습니다. 많은 서방 측 지도자들이 당황했습니다. 독일 헬무트 콜 총리는 고르바초프를 일단 선전술의 귀재로 보았습니다. 미심쩍어하면서도 큰 틀의 역사적 화해를 생각했습니다. 콜 총리는 한 인터뷰에서 나치의 괴벨스도 선전술의 대가였다고 언급했습니다. 물론 비보도...

items.snippet: ‘국중박(국립중앙박물관) 분장놀이’에 대한 반응이 이렇게 뜨거울 줄 몰랐다. 발랄하고 개성 넘치는 올해의 대상 수상자와 더불어 청화백자 잉어 모양 연적의 인기도 절정에 올랐기에, 이 기회를 빌려 청화백자 한 점을 소개해보려 한다.

items.title: “당신은 우리 편인가, 남의 편인가”… 연예인 정치색 따지는 사회
items.snippet: #1. “혹시 박진영 위원장은 저쪽에 섰나.” 7일 국회 문화체육관광위원회 국정감사에서 조은희 국민의힘 의원이 박진영 대중문화교류위원회 공동위원장에게 이렇게 말하자, 박 위원장은 두 손으로 얼굴을 감싸며 실소를 보였다. 조 의원은 박 위원장이 이재명 대통령과 함께 찍은 사진을 언급하며 “(박 위원장의) 명성이 이 정권의 흥망과 같이 가는 것 아닌가, 걱정을 하게 됐다”고 말했다. 이에 박 위원장은 “이 정권이나 민주당을 위해 일한다는 생각은 1초도 해본 적이 없다”고 해명했다.

items.title: 우리의 밤은 당신의 낮보다 아름답다
items.snippet: 파리 몽마르트르의 밤을 누군가의 이름으로 기억한다면 단연 앙리 드 툴루즈 로트레크(1864~1901)일 것이다. 화려한 무대, 객석의 웃음소리, 술잔 위로 내려앉은 짙은 피로까지 그가 캔버스에 담아낸 장면들은 지금도 당대의 환희를 생생히 되살린다. 전설적인 카바레 ‘물랭 루주’가 오늘날에도 그의 이름을 딴 툴루즈 로트레크 메뉴를 선보이며 경의를 표하는 까닭이며 세상이 그에게 ‘몽마르트르의 혼’이라는 찬사를 바치는 이유다. 부유한 귀족 출신 화가는 어쩌다 무희와 가수, 거리의 여성들이 살아가는 밤의 환락가를 그리게 됐을까? 그 배경에 샹송 가수 아리스티드 브뤼앙(1851~1925)이 있었다.

items.title: 알고 보면 역사가 길지 않은 각국 대표 음식들
items.snippet: 다양한 외국 음식이 우리 식단을 더 풍성하게 만들고 있다. 그런데 오랜 세월 이어져 왔을 것 같은 각국 대표 음식 중에 의외로 역사가 길지 않은 경우가 많다. 미국을 상징하는 햄버거는 19세기 말 독일 이주민들이 함부르크 스타일로 구운 스테이크를 넣어 팔던 네모난 샌드위치에서 유래했다. 오늘날의 형태를 갖춘 건 1916년 동그란 모양의 햄버거용 번이 나오면서부터였고 1950년대 맥도날드·버거킹 같은 대형 프랜차이즈가 성장하면서 미 전역으로 확산됐다.

items.title: 화산이 만든 천상의 습지… 100㎏ 짐 메고 목도를 걷는 ‘짐꾼 수행자’를 만나다
items.snippet: 2016년 여름 늦은 밤, 귀가를 신고하듯 습관처럼 TV를 켰다. 광활한 초록 속 끝없는 목도, 자기 키만 한 짐을 진 짐꾼이 그 길을 걷고 있었다. 구도자처럼 보였다. 박혁지 감독의 다큐멘터리 ‘길 위의 인생-인생을 짊어지고, 일본 봇카(歩荷)’였다. ‘오제(尾瀬)’는 ‘천상의 화원’이라 불린다는데, 예쁜 발음이라 마음에 쏙 새겨졌다.

items.title: “녹음합니다, 저를 지킬 최후의 보루니까요”
items.snippet: 정구승 법무법인 일로 대표 변호사는 최근 사건 의뢰를 받으면 가장 먼저 던지는 질문이 있다. 바로 사건의 ‘녹음 증거’를 가지고 있느냐는 것. 정 변호사는 “가정폭력이나 사기, 성범죄처럼 외부에 잘 드러나지 않는 범행에 휘말린 경우에는 자신에게 유리한 녹취록을 수사기관에 제출하는 게 필수”라며 “안 그래도 사건이 몰려 처리가 느린 경찰이 보완수사까지 떠맡게 되면서 피의자와 피해자 모두 공정하고 빠른 종결을 위해 사건 실체를 담은 녹음 증거 수집이 더 중요해졌다”고 말했다.

items.title: 어제보다 먼 곳으로
items.snippet: 자동차 업계가 자율주행 기술 주도권을 놓고 치열한 경쟁을 벌이고 있습니다. 운전자가 핸들이나 페달을 조작하지 않아도 자동차가 스스로 목적지까지 찾아가게 하는 기술 말이죠. 그런데 이 기술이 정말 절실한 곳은 지구가 아니라 화성인지도 모르겠습니다.

items.title: 떡 먹으려고 KTX 탄다… 2030 ‘떡지순례’ 열풍
items.snippet: 13일 오전 9시 30분 롯데백화점 잠실점 지하 식품관 입구. 문이 열리려면 한 시간이나 남았지만 이미 72명이 대기 중이었다. 이들은 지난 9일부터 15일까지 열린 ‘전국 떡지순례’ 팝업 행사의 입장 번호표를 받기 위해 새벽부터 집을 나섰다. 줄 맨 앞에 선 남성은 “오전 7시 15분에 도착했다”고 했다. 오전 10시 30분이 되자 대기 인원은 200명을 넘었다. 백화점 관계자는 “일부 인기 떡집은 오후 1시 준비한 떡이 다 팔려 조기 마감할 정도”라며 “떡의 인기를 실감하고 있다”고 했다.

items.title: 미야자키 하야오도 반한 이끼의 섬
items.snippet: 오제를 걷다 보면 때때로 깊은 산을 통과해야 할 때가 있다. 길은 가파른데 유혹하는 것들이 많다. 삼나무와 이끼다. 그러나 오제의 이끼를 ‘최고’라 말하진 않겠다. 이끼라면 역시 야쿠시마(屋久島) 아닌가. 오제보다 석 달 먼저 방문한 ‘야쿠시마’를 소환하는 이유다. 가고시마현 남단의 섬, 야쿠시마는 제주도의 4분의 1 정도 면적으로 원시림을 비롯한 산악 지역이 1993년 유네스코 세계자연유산에 등재됐다.

items.title: 짧고 굵게, 아파트 명칭도 재건축 바람
items.snippet: 이름에는 당대의 미감이 담긴다. 이를테면 1970년대 지어진 서울 서초 신동아1·2차아파트는 반세기 전 작명 규칙에 충실한 이름이었다. 지난해 재건축 공사에 돌입해 곧 고급 주거 단지로 천지개벽할 이 아파트, 새 이름이 관건이었다. 2017년 건설사가 제시한 건 ‘아크로 클라우드 파크’였다. 구름 위 천상 공원. 건설사 브랜드 뒤에 거창한 펫네임(petname·별칭)을 붙이는, 10년 전 유행에 부합하는 이름. 그랬던 이름은 2022년 ‘아크로 드 서초’로 확 줄었고, 지난 4월 한 글자가 더 줄어 ‘아크로 서초’로 최종 확정됐다.

items.title: 우리는 AI를 웃길 수 있을까
items.snippet: 우리는 매일 수많은 사회 현상을 마주합니다. 빠르게 번지는 유행, 집단적 쏠림 현상, 그리고 이해하기 어려운 선택의 반복…. 사람들은 왜 그렇게 생각하고 행동하는 걸까요? 인지심리학자인 김경일 아주대 심리학과 교수가 겉으로 드러난 현상 이면에 작동하는 기제가 개인의 선택과 집단의 움직임에 어떤 영향을 미치는지 짚어봅니다. – 편집자 주

items.title: 한국에서는 왜 노벨 과학상 수상자가 안 나올까
items.snippet: “우리나라에선 언제쯤 노벨상이 나올까?” 이런 말을 하는 분들이 꽤 많다. 이웃 일본이 거의 매년 노벨상을 받으며 ‘엄친아’ 역할을 하고 있으니, 박탈감이 더 클 수밖에 없다. 물론 우리나라에서도 노벨상이 두 번 나왔다. 2000년 김대중 전 대통령이 평화상을, 2024년에는 한강 작가가 문학상을 탔다. 두 분의 수상은 높이 평가받아야 하지만, 그런데도 우리가 계속 노벨상 타령을 하는 것은 과학 분야 수상자가 나오지 않아서다. 과학 분야 노벨상(이하 과학상)이야말로 국력의 정도를 보여주는 지표이기 때문이다.

items.title: Water-Energy-Data nexus reveals sustainability gaps and priorities for AI infrastructure
items.abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) depends on interconnected water, energy, and data systems spanning infrastructure life cycles and diverse geographies, with the potential to intensify water and energy insecurity, exacerbate social inequities and lead to cascading sustainability issues globally. items.title: Hydrogen Ion-Cut Single-Crystal Diamond Membranes for Wide and Ultrawide Bandgap Semiconductor Heterointegration
items.abstract: Single-crystal diamond membranes (SCDms) were created using a hydrogen ion-cut process combined with a two-step post-implantation annealing, electrochemical etching, and micro-transfer printing. Monte Carlo simulations comparing H, He, C, and O implantation predicted a narrower vacancy-distribution profile for hydrogen under the implantation conditions examined. Raman spectroscopy was used to evaluate implantation-induced lattice damage and its recovery during annealing and membrane release, while optical bandgap analysis provided further evidence of restoration of the diamond lattice structure. After delamination and removal of residual graphitic material, freestanding SCDms with improved crystalline quality were obtained. items.title: From Surface Reactions to Inhibitor Coverage: A Machine-Learning-Assisted Computational Study of Area-Selective Atomic Layer Deposition
items.abstract: Area-selective atomic layer deposition (AS-ALD) enables selective material growth for the fabrication of nanoscale semiconductor devices. Predicting inhibitor coverage is essential for understanding and optimizing surface blocking in AS-ALD. Here, we present a computational workflow combining a pretrained universal machine-learning interatomic potential with off-lattice grand canonical Monte Carlo simulations and apply it to inhibitor adsorption and precursor blocking on amorphous SiO2. Realistic surface models reveal substantial site-dependent variations in reaction energies and activation barriers, with silanol groups serving as the primary adsorption sites for aminosilane and related inhibitors and metal precursors. items.title: Coherent phonons in photoexcited semiconductors from first principles
items.abstract: Coherent phonons are phase-locked lattice vibrations that provide a sensitive probe of nonequilibrium dynamics in materials. Existing first-principles equation-of-motion (EOM) approaches have successfully described coherent phonons in metals and semimetals, but their extension to semiconductors requires treating the long-lived electron--hole plasma created by above-gap excitation. Here we extend the first-principles EOM framework to photoexcited semiconductors by incorporating the residual plasma force that shifts the lattice equilibrium together with the plasma-induced renormalization of the electronic structure. For monolayer MoTe$_2$, the calculated carrier-density-dependent Te displacement agrees with constrained density-functional perturbation theory only when the renormalized band structure is included. items.title: Programmable Preparation of Topological Entangled States
items.abstract: Programmable preparation of entangled quantum states is a central requirement for scalable quantum information processing, quantum networking and photonic quantum computing. Topological photonic platforms offer an attractive route towards robust quantum-state generation by encoding information in symmetry- protected optical modes, yet the generated entangled states are typically dictated by the lattice geometry and therefore lack programmability. Here we demonstrate programmable preparation of topological entangled states by inverse engineering the nonlinear optical pump profile of an integrated photonic lattice. Our approach enables deterministic control over both the dimensionality and modal structure of the generated entangled state while preserving its topological character. items.title: Trapping of nanofabricated SiO$_2$ high-aspect-ratio discs in an optical lattice
items.abstract: We describe the nanofabrication and loading of lithographically patterned, high aspect ratio $10$ $μ$m diameter silicon dioxide discs with thickness of $400$ nm into an optical standing wave trap in vacuum. We obtain motional spectra of the center of mass motion of the discs using a combination of interferometric and imaging methods. The method is capable of high-efficiency loading and optical trapping using small numbers of objects, of the order of a few particles, with customized geometries and sizes compatible with wafer scale nanofabrication methods. Disc-like particles in optical traps have been identified as promising candidates for detectors of high frequency gravitational waves or as sensitive accelerometers.

items.title: Extended strange metal and superconductivity in partially filled moiré Hubbard bands
items.abstract: Moiré semiconductors provide a physical realization of the Hubbard model. Bandwidth-tuned Mott transitions and complex phase diagrams mimicking those of high-temperature superconductors have been demonstrated near a weak Mott insulating state at half-band-filling. The platform also provides an opportunity to explore the physics of a partially filled Hubbard band at doping densities far away from the Mott insulator, a regime that has remained largely unexplored. items.title: Enabling large language model agents for high-fidelity many-body perturbation theory calculations
items.abstract: Many-body perturbation theory (MBPT) methods, including the GW approximation, the GW plus Bethe-Salpeter equation (GW-BSE) method, and GW perturbation theory (GWPT), among others, provide accurate first-principles descriptions of excited-state properties and multiparticle interactions of materials. However, their use remains limited due to complex multi-software workflows, interdependent physical parameters, and substantial theoretical expertise. Large language model (LLM) agents, which couple a language model to software tools, show potential in automating computational tasks, but MBPT remains an unaddressed challenge. We show that LLM agents tested in our work, including frontier models such as Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.5, do not reliably construct MBPT workflows in one attempt, suggesting that correct setup requires expert knowledge and consistency that current models lack. items.title: Robust Data-Driven Controller Synthesis from Sampled and Uncertain Frequency Response Estimates using Integral Quadratic Constraints
items.abstract: In this paper, we develop a novel MIMO controller synthesis method that relies solely on frequency-domain data of discrete-time systems. The approach is based on an iterative design procedure using \emph{integral quadratic constraints} (IQCs). It generalizes existing data-driven methods that approximate semi-infinite IQC conditions by enforcing them on a finite set of measured frequency points. Such approximations do not provide guarantees on the continuous frequency axis and may fail to capture inter-frequency behavior. We address this limitation by formulating a convex optimization problem that preserves robustness guarantees over the entire frequency range. In particular, the proposed method explicitly accounts for inter-frequency behavior of both plant and controller, leading to certified robust stability and performance. The effectiveness and computational efficiency of the approach...

items.title: The Reciprocal tau-Cell: A Log-Domain Circuit for On-Chip Learning
items.abstract: Training hardware by gradient descent requires a gradient to be computed using a separate backwards pass. If a circuit is reciprocal, meaning every connection is symmetric, the backward pass is the same network run a second time with the error as its input. The reciprocal tau-cell, a weak-inversion log-domain circuit, makes this practical in standard CMOS. Each cell is a current-mode leaky integrator with a built-in ReLU; each connection is two transistors whose signed strength is a ratio of bias currents. The equilibrium of the network is the solution to a convex program, and latching the cells that are off will hardware linearise the circuit, making its second run exactly linear. items.title: On-sky performance and prospects of near-infrared CMOS detectors in exoplanet detection: first year of SPIRIT
items.abstract: Ultracool dwarfs are promising targets for detecting and characterising temperate terrestrial exoplanets. Their flux peaks in the near-infrared, beyond the wavelength cut-off of the silicon-based CCDs used by ground-based surveys dedicated to observing them, such as SPECULOOS. We present the on-sky performance of SPIRIT (SPeculoos InfraRed Imager for Transits), an InGaAs CMOS detector on the Callisto telescope at the SPECULOOS Southern Observatory, during its first year of operation, from mid-2022 to 2023. We use 328 visits of 73 targets to optimise our CMOS-specific reduction process, including our approach to glow effects and bad-pixel handling. We find the measured precision to be consistent with our theoretical noise model, achieving sub-part-per-thousand precision under good observing conditions across targets spanning $J$-band magnitudes of 10--13. items.title: CAFE: Conducting-Cell-Aware Adaptive Differential Encoding for Robust DNN Inference in FeFET-Based Compute-in-Memory
items.abstract: Ferroelectric field-effect transistor (FeFET)-based compute-in-memory (CIM) promises energy-efficient deep neural network (DNN) inference, but device variation can severely degrade bit-sliced CIM accuracy. Prior works either rely on hardware modifications or treat such variation as generic noise, overlooking a key FeFET asymmetry: negligible off-state leakage makes errors dominated by conducting on-state cells. This asymmetry is amplified by two's-complement sign extension, which maps small negative values to high-significance bit slices and magnifies their errors during shift-and-add reconstruction. In this paper, we propose CAFE, a conducting-cell-aware adaptive differential encoding framework built upon this FeFET-specific asymmetry. CAFE introduces C$^2$AM, a bit-significance-weighted conducting-cell activity metric that predicts output deviation and inference accuracy degradation un...

items.title: Pressure engineering of the excitonic moiré-potential landscape and exciton-charge interplay in semiconductor moiré superlattices
items.abstract: Semiconductor moiré superlattices, owing to strongly bound excitons and pronounced electronic correlation, have emerged as an intriguing solid platform for exploring correlated bosonic phenomena, where the moiré potential landscape plays a central role. Hydrostatic pressure allows continuous, in-situ tuning of this landscape, but remains underexplored because of experimental challenges. Here we integrate a diamond anvil pressure cell with high quality dual gated WSe2/WS2 twisted bilayers and perform cryogenic optical spectroscopy. We observe distinct pressure evolutions of moiré intralayer excitons, which reveal drastic modulation of the excitonic moiré-potential landscape captured by a continuum model and suggest the capability of engineering the exciton-band topology. items.abstract: We propose CktHGVAE, a heterogeneous graph variational autoencoder for transistor-level analog/mixedsignal CMOS circuits that takes not only design variables but also state variables as its inputs and outputs. Latent-space optimization in the PCA-reduced latent space with Bayesian optimization, evolutionary search, random search, and quasi-exhaustive search is demonstrated for a common-source voltage amplifier with NMOS input and resistive load, where the objective function is defined as a penalty for deviation from required circuit specifications. items.abstract: Tracing my scientific path from many-body physics in semiconductor nanostructures to topological quantum matter, this Habilitation à diriger des recherches (HDR) memoir presents only part of my research since defending two PhD theses in Toulouse and Nizhny Novgorod in 2011. items.abstract: Strong coupling between mobile charge carriers or excitons and lattice vibrations gives rise to polarons: quasiparticles formed by charge carriers dressed by a cloud of phonon excitations. Polaron formation determines transport properties of systems ranging from transition-metal oxides and organic semiconductors to light-harvesting complexes. In excitonic systems that admit a hard-core boson description, mapping the excitations to pseudospins provides a natural framework for studying polaron physics, including the nonperturbative regime in which hopping amplitudes, phonon energies, and coupling strengths are comparable. items.title: Single anyons and anyon binding in a quantum Hall dot
items.abstract: Anyons are particles with quantized fractional statistics. In theory, a single anyon can be stabilized as a localized fractional charge within the bulk of a topologically ordered two-dimensional insulator. However, experiments to date have focused on probing anyons in structures in which many anyonic excitations coexist and interact. Here, we demonstrate the trapping of a single anyon in a device consisting of a graphene-based quantum point contact with an embedded tunable quantum Hall dot. Benchmarking our device at v = 1, we demonstrate backscattering between Fermi liquid edge states mediated by the whole-electron Coulomb blockade of the dot. The cleanliness and control available in our device allow depletion of the dot to the last quasihole, and we observe spin blockade for transitions to the opposite-spin Landau level. items.abstract: Ultrafast laser excitation of carriers in semiconductors often results in the creation of fully symmetric coherent optical phonons, typically understood in terms of a thermalized transient carrier population. We test this understanding with systematic measurements and first-principles calculations of the photon-energy dependence of ultrafast-laser-driven coherent phonon generation in tellurium, using excitation wavelengths around the electronic band gap. We observe that, contrary to the expectations of models assuming a thermalized carrier population, the coherent amplitude of the fully symmetric $A_1$ mode changes only weakly when tuning wavelength across the band gap. The measured spectral dependence is instead reproduced by a transition-resolved prethermal force weighted by optical matrix elements and band- and momentum-dependent $A_1$ deformation potentials. items.title: Tellurium trioxide as an n-type wide-gap semiconductor with ultrahigh work functions from first principles
items.abstract: The exploration of next-generation wide-gap semiconductors with extreme work functions is highly desirable for the continued advancement of electronic and optoelectronic devices. By using first principles calculations, we show that \b{eta}-TeO3, with a wide band gap exceeding 3 eV, emerges as a promising n-type semiconductor exhibiting ultrahigh work functions of up to ~8 eV. Intentionally or unintentionally incorporated interstitial H, Li, Na, Cu, Mg, and Zn impurities and substitutional F impurities are identified as shallow donors, whereas O vacancies act as minor carrier-compensating defects that locally trap electrons at neighbouring Te sites. The work function is evaluated across a series of low-index nonpolar surfaces. items.abstract: While most studies on Co$2$MnAl (CMA) focus on the ultrathin regime for spintronic junctions, applications scaling with magnetic volume--such as Anomalous Nernst Effect (ANE) energy harvesters, integrated power inductors, and magnetic MEMS--require significantly thicker films. In this work, 750 nm thick CMA films were grown on MgO (001) and Si substrates to establish a roadmap for their thermal integration. Structural analysis reveals that B2 ordering is optimized on MgO at 600 $^\circ$C, which is important for functional devices. In contrast, samples on Si substrates exhibit a disorder transition toward the A2 phase, closely linked to diffusion-driven degradation processes. items.title: Theory of deeply subwavelength electromagnetic structuring of semiconductors due to thermal-ionization instability
items.abstract: We develop a theory of ionization-assisted instability that governs the reflection of intense electromagnetic pulses from a semiconductor surface. Local overheating of the material increases the free-carrier density and conductivity, which in turn enhances the absorption of the incident radiation and further amplifies local heating and avalanche ionization. At high pump repetition rates, the overheating accumulates from pulse to pulse, leading to a gradual rise of the local material temperature and free carrier density - a positive feedback loop that drives thermal runaway. However, this effect competes with diffraction of the pump field on the emerging perturbation of the dielectric permittivity or on the surface relief, which reduces the local electric field amplitude in the overheated regions, thus providing negative feedback. items.title: Mixed Precision Scaling Laws for Quantized Pretraining
items.abstract: Since scaling laws were introduced for modern LLMs (Kaplan et al., 2020), several works have extended them to account for quantization, tracking the emerging low-precision data types supported on AI accelerators. We develop a more accurate scaling law for quantized pretraining with mixed precision across the forward and backward passes, grounded in optimization theory and validated empirically. Our formulation separates the effects of quantization on model capacity and on optimization efficiency, and explicitly models the persistent optimization error from forward and backward quantization identified through convergence analysis. To select the regimes for fitting and evaluating our law, we first decompose existing 4-bit training recipes into their forward and backward components, isolating those that most affect loss. items.title: First-Principles Calculations of the Electron-Hole-Pair Creation Energy in Semiconductors and Dielectrics
items.abstract: We present first-principles calculations of the electron-hole-pair creation energy in semiconductors and dielectrics, focusing in particular on AlN, 3C-SiC, 4H-SiC, Si, and SiO2. We have employed density functional theory (DFT) to calculate the band structure, density-functional perturbation theory to obtain the phonon dispersion, and time-dependent DFT (TDDFT) to calculate the electron energy loss function (via the dielectric function). We performed full-band Monte Carlo simulations of electron thermalization for energies up to ~100 eV and calculated the average energy required to excite an electron-hole pair. We calculated pair-creation energies of approximately 12.2, 6.5, 7.3, 3.10, and 16.7 eV/pair for AlN, 3C-SiC, 4H-SiC, Si, and SiO2, respectively. items.title: Decoupling Trap States in Amorphous Oxide Semiconductor Transistor Using a Conductive-Semiconducting-Conductive MOS Structure
items.abstract: We propose a novel amorphous oxide semiconductor (AOS)-based conductive-semiconducting-conductive (CSC) MOS test structure to effectively sense, discriminate, and analyze distinct trap-induced conductance losses in AOS transistors. In conventional test structures, non-ideal metal-AOS contacts convolute the conductance loss generated by various trap states. The CSC architecture mitigates these contact-related artifacts, enabling the decoupling of interface states and shallow states. Furthermore, the contributions from leakage, series resistance, and device-geometry effects are identified and calibrated. Our results yield bias-resolved trap profiles and reveal three distinct regimes: (1) In the depletion region, interface states dominate the conductance loss. These states exhibit sub-microsecond time constants and their density increases slightly with deeper depletion, which is associated...

items.title: Toward Partitioned Reference Readout for Four-Level IGZO Memory: Device Statistics, Confusion Matrices, and INT4 Error Propagation
items.abstract: Four-level indium-gallium-zinc oxide (IGZO) 2T0C memory needs reliable state formation, sensing references, and a path from cell errors to digital weights. We analyze 107 measured DC transfer curves from 37 isolated IGZO transistors (W/L = 3/0.5 micrometers). Four gate-bias operating points inferred from the first sweep are evaluated on later sweeps of 35 devices. Device-resolved operating points reduce second-sweep across-device current standard deviation by 49.4-52.4%, yet retaining initial thresholds increases misclassified points from 37/140 to 55/140. Leave-one-device-out reference estimation gives 0/140 on the second sweep; freezing second-sweep thresholds yields 6/140 on the third. Sampling eight reference transistors on the third sweep gives a mean held-out error fraction of 0.15% over 2,000 selections, versus 4.33% with frozen thresholds on matched held-out devices. We present c...

items.title: Transfer learning-aided, artificial intelligence approach to evaluate optical properties of materials for classical and quantum photonic applications
items.abstract: In this study, an artificial intelligence-assisted evaluation of the refractive indices of different materials is performed. The evaluation of the refractive index is necessary to design photonic devices for various classical and quantum photonic applications, and to theoretically analyse experimental results. The refractive index is one of the crucial parameters that affect the interaction of light with matter. Although the refractive index can be measured experimentally, its estimation via computational means provide the advantage of not requiring costly instrumentation, trained researchers and could avoid potential laboratory-based uncertainties. Therefore, in this study, artificial intelligence is implemented to estimate the optical constants of two types of materials, i.e., noble metals, and semiconductors. To this end, an artificial neural network is used to estimate the real and t...

items.title: Stateless Stochastic Computing for Generative AI on Superconducting Logic: A Model-Hardware Co-Design
items.abstract: Thermodynamic computing lets stochastic physical dynamics carry out a computation and reads out the result as a time average. Recently, thermodynamic computing has been demonstrated on several hardware platforms, including digital CMOS circuits based on stochastic computing. Superconducting single-flux-quantum (SFQ) logic offers very high clock rates and very low switching energy, but it heavily penalizes state, memory, fan-out, and feedback, i.e., exactly the per-neuron accumulators on which such designs rely. We therefore realize thermodynamic computing in SFQ logic through a co-design of a generative model and its circuit in which the datapath holds no state at all. The model is a class-conditional flow-matching image generator, which transforms Gaussian noise into an image of the requested class along a short, deterministic path of four Euler steps; in hardware, these steps are unrol...

items.title: The Era of Vibe Tapeout: Dark Age or Golden Age for Analog Circuit Design?
items.abstract: LLM agents now write their own schematic and layout generators, run EDA tools, read the results, and fix the design. This "vibe tapeout" is becoming practical for analog circuits as well. This paper measures how far it has come in two settings. (A) On an open PDK (SKY130), a cloud LLM agent designed an 11-bit, 5.12-MS/s SAR ADC from its specification. The agents produced DRC- and LVS-clean macros and met the specification after parasitic extraction (PEX). In particular, under the condition in which the agent received a sanitized reference design derived from our 65-nm design (vibe porting), it produced the best layout in the shortest time. Its area was 1/1.6 to 1/2.8 of that of the conditions without a reference. This condition reached signoff without human intervention. The agents also identified the causes of post-PEX degradation (CDAC wiring coupling and common-mode-dependent comparat...

items.title: Localized Joule heating and carbonization process optimization of 3D printed polymer structures for lab-on-CMOS applications
items.abstract: Use of carbon electrodes integrated with CMOS technology has great promise for lab-on-chip, biomedical, environmental, and industrial applications. One method of developing carbon electrodes is to 3D print polymer nanostructures on a CMOS chip, and use a thermal annealing process to pyrolyze them into carbon at high temperature, approximately 950 °C. Such high temperature is detrimental to the CMOS sensor circuits, causing severe degradation. We present a novel solution of localized Joule heating of these polymer nanostructures to achieve complete carbonization of the electrodes. Both analytical and COMSOL simulations guided the experiments to characterize the carbonization process conditions. Partial carbonization was achieved at 500-600 °C of global temperature, and complete carbonization was achieved by localized Joule heating. items.title: TileCas: Cascading Kernel Development Across Programming Abstractions
items.abstract: Programming abstractions have traditionally been designed for humans, but code generation is increasingly performed by models and autonomous agents. We investigate abstractions for machine-driven programming through GPU and AI-accelerator kernel generation. High-level domain-specific languages (DSLs) simplify search by delegating implementation details to compilers, while lower-level representations provide finer-grained control at the cost of a larger and more complex search space. In this paper, we present TileCas, a unified, pluggable interface that enables coding agents to develop kernels across multiple editable abstraction levels. Rather than committing to a single representation, TileCas allows an agent to transfer and refine candidates across levels through Cross-Level Diagnosis, which maps correctness and performance feedback to actionable controls at different abstraction level...

items.title: Enhancing Quasi-Two-Dimensional Electronic Structure in Bi2O2Se via Chlorine Substitution
items.abstract: Bismuth oxyselenide (Bi2O2Se) has emerged as a leading semiconductor candidate for next-generation electronics and quantum phenomena research. However, its strong ionic interlayer bonding of Se layers fundamentally restricts the full potential of this otherwise promising quasi-two-dimensional (2D) material. In this work, we demonstrate chlorine substitution as an effective strategy to introduce van der Waals gaps and modify the electronic structure of the system. Through comprehensive transport and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) measurements on Bi6O6Se2Cl2 single crystal, an optimal Cl-doping compound, we show that the key electronic features, including indirect band gap, high electron mobility, and carrier effective mass, are well preserved, while the 2D character of the system is sufficiently enhanced. First-principles calculations attribute this selective tunability...

AI Acceleration of Muon Collider R&D: A Report from the AI4MuC Workshop
items.abstract: A Muon Collider is one of the most attractive routes to multi-TeV lepton collisions, but it requires the accelerator and detector communities to solve a tightly coupled set of problems that have no close precedent in an operating collider. Muons must be produced, captured, cooled, accelerated, and collided before they decay. The detector must then extract clean physics from an environment dominated by decay products from the beamline. Artificial intelligence is not a substitute for accelerator physics, detector design, or engineering validation. It is, however, unusually well matched to several of the central obstacles: high-dimensional design spaces, expensive simulations, coupled subsystem trade-offs, and workflows that are currently too slow or too fragile to support broad design exploration. This report distills the AI4MuC workshop into a summary of AI use cases with the potential to...

items.title: Revealing New Leakage Paths in GAAFETs using Predictive First-Principles Simulations
items.abstract: Gate-All-Around Field-Effect Transistors (GAAFETs) are emerging as successors to Fin Field-Effect Transistors (FinFETs) and are central to continued scaling at advanced semiconductor nodes. Despite their improved electrostatic control, recent measurements show that the drain current in GAAFETs deviates strongly from thermionic behavior at negative gate voltages, increasing as the gate voltage becomes more negative. This leakage has been attributed to direct gate-drain tunneling through the high-$k$ dielectric, enhanced by drain-induced dielectric barrier lowering (DIDBL). Here, we use predictive, charge-self-consistent Non-Equilibrium Green Function (NEGF) simulations based on the Contact Block Reduction (CBR) method to spatially resolve this leakage pathway in GAAFETs. Unlike approaches based primarily on phenomenological leakage models, our first-principles, multi-terminal quantum-tran...

items.title: DFIT: A Framework for Building Instrumentation Tools Across Heterogeneous Dataflow Accelerators
items.abstract: Emerging dataflow accelerators offer exceptional energy efficiency and throughput for machine learning workloads, yet remain largely opaque to developers for performance analysis. Unlike CPUs and GPUs, where instrumentation frameworks enable fine-grained introspection, dataflow hardware exposes little information. This lack of transparency limits the ability of compiler engineers, system designers, and application developers to analyze, tune, or debug accelerator behavior. In this paper, we introduce DFIT (DataFlow Accelerator Instrumentation Tool), an instrumentation framework designed specifically for dataflow architectures. DFIT directly instruments operations, regions, and compiler transformations at the graph IR and backend-lowering stages using semantic program representation. DFIT captures high-level, semantically meaningful data that reflect the true dataflow of computation. Thes...

items.title: Predicting Nanofabrication Variance: A Conditional Diffusion Model
items.abstract: Micro- and nanostructures fabricated by focused ion beam (FIB) milling invariably deviate from input designs due to systematic and stochastic effects such as ablation-rate fluctuations, and redeposition. As such, nominally identical iterations of a given process yield a distribution of non-identical fabrication outcomes, leading to variations in the physical (optical, mechanical) properties of fabricated structures. Existing models of the milling process typically predict a single deterministic fabrication result, neglecting this variability. Here we present a conditional diffusion model that learns the statistical distribution of process outcomes conditioned on input design, enabling it to predict a realistic distribution of possible output sample structures. These predictions accurately reproduce edge morphology, linewidth variations, and defect probabilities observed in fabricated sam...

items.title: Bottom-Up Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering for the Detection of Micro-Objects and Globular Analytes
items.abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is typically achieved by depositing the analyte on a metal or semiconductor substrate. We propose a bottom-up approach, enabling SERS by depositing a metal on the surface of the object being studied. A Mie-theory analysis of electric-field enhancement in dielectric core-shell particles is presented. A correlative approach combining SERS, atomic force microscopy, and scanning electron microscopy is employed to model the conditions required for sensitive SERS detection and spectral analysis of polystyrene microspheres (PMSs) as models of globular and vesicle-like objects. Based on these findings, we propose a SERS-active system that provides strong signal enhancement (up to four orders of magnitude for a single globular object) while maintaining spectral fidelity, where PMSs act both as model analytes and as integral components of a metal-dielectric...

items.title: Theory of exciton-exciton interactions in crystalline systems
items.abstract: Excitons are bound electron-hole pairs in semiconductors whose interactions influence optical properties and determine their collective behavior and emergent correlated phases. Despite the theoretical and experimental significance of these phenomena, a microscopic theory of exciton-exciton interactions that takes into account the full composite nature of these quasiparticles is lacking. Here, we present a general theory of exciton-exciton interactions that builds upon our previous publication [Physical Review B 113, 155440 (2026)], which applied only to conventional semiconductors with weak band hybridization. By contrast, the theory presented here is valid in virtually any crystalline semiconducting system and can be applied to the study of biexciton formation and correlated excitonic phases in systems where band topology, quantum geometry, and moiré effects play a significant role. items.title: Orbital transfer reveals material-selective structure in Rydberg excitons
items.abstract: Rydberg excitons in atomically thin semiconductors offer a sensitive view of dielectric screening and electronic structure. As their spectra become increasingly well resolved, a central question is how much material information an effective Hamiltonian can predict beyond the states used to determine it. Using the 1s, 2p and 2s levels to determine a scalar Rytova-Keldysh Hamiltonian, we test its transfer to the excluded 3p state. The transfer deviations have opposite signs: the observed 3p lies 7.38 meV below the prediction in MoSe2 and 5.58 meV above it in WS2; the opposite signs persist across the complete reported +/-2-sigma peak-error boxes. In a separate high-field-calibrated benchmark, RK removes 66.8% of the orbital error of a pure two-dimensional Coulomb reference, making the remaining state-selective deviations particularly informative. items.title: Evolution and breakdown of chiral anomaly in Weyl semiconductor tellurium
items.abstract: Chiral anomaly in topological materials manifests as negative longitudinal magnetoresistance, yet the tunability and evolution of this effect remain elusive. Here we show that doped tellurium serves as a versatile platform to realize a giant negative longitudinal magnetoresistance that is highly tunable via the Fermi level and magnetic field. By moving the Fermi level towards the Weyl point, we observe a pronounced enhancement of negative magnetoresistance, which arises from chiral anomaly and robustly persists up to ambient temperature. Beyond the quantum limit, the system exhibits positive linear magnetoconductance, serving as a compelling transport signature of the chiral anomaly in the lowest Landau level. Notably, in the extreme quantum limit at cryogenic temperatures, the magnetoresistance undergoes a dramatic reversal from negative to positive. This reversal points to a potential...

items.title: From Prompts to Silicon: Scaling LLM-Assisted Chip Design with the AI Hardware Design League
items.abstract: The semiconductor workforce shortage has renewed interest in making chip design accessible to students without conventional very-large-scale integration (VLSI) training. We present the AI Hardware Design League (AI-HDL), an international, project-based competition in which students use Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate and iteratively refine Verilog while simulation, synthesis, timing analysis, security review, and physical verification provide the engineering feedback needed to validate the result. Across two annual cycles, AI-HDL grew from 172 to 604 participants and from 40 to 108 teams, reaching 30 universities, six community colleges, and 19 countries. In the 2026 cohort, 68.7% of participants reported no prior Verilog experience. Twenty-two teams completed the four design phases and reached final evaluation. Two division-winning designs completed physical sign-off in the Sky...

items.title: Nonlocal Josephson coupling and current redistribution in a large-area graphene multiterminal Josephson junction
items.abstract: Multiterminal Josephson junctions (MTJJs) extend conventional two-terminal Josephson physics to devices defined by multiple superconducting phases, where rich phenomena have been predicted. However, in conventional MTJJs, superconducting transport is often dominated by local coupling between neighboring leads, obscuring physics that goes beyond simple connectivity. Here, we realize a multiterminal Josephson network in a graphene Hall bar geometry with micron-scale dimensions, enabling substantial nonlocal coupling between distant terminals. Our key observation is a pronounced negative differential longitudinal resistance (NDLR) in the four-probe response near switching currents, while no such feature appears in two-terminal measurements. items.title: Measuring the Speed of Light with a Time-of-Flight Setup: An Authentic Experiment for High School
items.abstract: Students often perceive scientific experiments as clean, straightforward procedures with predictable outcomes. Students' beliefs about the nature of experimental physics typically remain inconsistent through the initial stages of undergraduate education. In reality, experimental work in physics involves hands-on activities such as soldering circuits, assembling provisional setups, and building functional mock-ups from simple materials before reliable measurements can be achieved. To address this gap, we designed a laboratory activity in which students were completely involved in the experiment design, construction and operation with the final goal of measuring the speed of light with a low-cost and compact setup. items.abstract: Most systems trained by equilibrium propagation or coupled learning are in the same class as multi-layer perceptrons: while they may be universal function approximators, they struggle to learn associative tasks which are easy for transformers. Equilibrium propagation relies on a bidirectional flow of information through the physical system between input and output. The reverse flow is broken by more complex nonlinear systems, such as those performing multiplication which is needed to express dot-product attention. Here we explicitly restore this bidirectional flow by introducing extra circuit elements for this purpose into a double or dyadic circuit. We then use these ideas to construct an attention mechanism exploiting the exponential current law of sub-threshold MOSFET devices. items.title: Spatiotemporal computing for temporal nonlinear tasks using few-mode fiber and SOA nonlinearity
items.abstract: Step-index few-mode fibers (FMFs) provide a compact passive platform for high-speed photonic information processing by exploiting modal dispersion to map temporal inputs into spatiotemporal representations with short-term memory. In previous studies, we have demonstrated linear classification tasks with such FMFs, such as ultrafast multibit header recognition. Here, we extend the computational capability of such architectures towards solving nonlinear tasks by introducing an optical nonlinearity at the output of the dispersive medium. The FMF output is processed through parallel direct and nonlinear branches, with the latter implemented using a nonlinear semiconductor optical amplifier (SOA). We experimentally evaluate the architecture at 28.5 Gb/s on two delayed XOR and higher-order parity tasks. items.title: Effects of chlorine substitution on the magneto-optical properties of CrSBr
items.abstract: We present a systematic study of the effects of chlorine substitution on the magneto-optical properties of the van der Waals layered semiconductor CrSBr. Our study shows that even at substitution level of $x=56\%$ the $\mathrm{CrSBr_{1-x}Cl_{x}}$ material exhibits qualitatively the same clear magneto-optical coupling that was observed in pure CrSBr crystals. The values of the relevant parameters are shown to vary smoothly across different substitution levels, thus offering promising tunability for this family of 2D magnetic materials.

items.abstract: Quantum technologies witness rapid contemporary developments transitioning from abstract scientific ideas and fundamental demonstrations, into systems of sufficient quality and scale, enabling real applications. Photonic quantum technologies are playing a pivotal role in these developments, since photons are robust, easily controlled, detect and measured, thus qualify as flying carriers of quantum information and entanglement distributers. The efforts to develop photonic quantum technologies benefit from the maturity of the classical optical technologies. It was shown that even a source of heralded three entangled photons is sufficient for building large scale quantum computers using otherwise classical optical elements. items.abstract: Two dimensional Janus semiconductors integrating spin-valley coupling, piezoelectricity, and tunable optical responses offer a platform for multifunctional nanodevices. Here, first-principles calculations reveal complementary composition and strain effects in CrSiCN4 and CrGeCN4 monolayers. Both are found to be nonmagnetic direct-gap semiconductors, with gaps of 1.23 and 1.09 eV using the Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof functional including spin-orbit coupling, respectively. HSE06 hybrid-functional calculations retain the direct-gap character, yielding gaps of 1.46 eV for CrSiCN4 and 1.19 eV for CrGeCN4. Opposite out-of-plane spin character and Berry curvature emerge at K and K'. ATLAS: Adaptive TDA-guided Landscape-Aware Transistor Sizing
items.abstract: Analog transistor sizing, finding design parameters that simultaneously satisfy multiple performance specifications, is a labor-intensive bottleneck in circuit design. To support analog circuit experts, various automation methods have been proposed, including Bayesian optimization (BO), reinforcement learning (RL), and others. Yet existing methods are oblivious to the topological structure of a feasible design space, which can fragment into disconnected regions due to operating-regime transitions, conflicting specification trade-offs, and nonconvex device physics. This topological blindness causes the optimizer to converge within a single feasible region while missing others that may contain superior designs. items.abstract: We propose that the path to realizing the full potential of two-dimensional (2D) electronics lies in understanding and mastering their energy band tail states (BTS). Unlike silicon, which benefits from sharp band edges (Urbach energy $E_\rm U$ ~ 10 meV), today's monolayer 2D semiconductors have rough band edges ($E_\rm U$ ~ 100 meV) caused by spatial potential inhomogeneity. Comparing a physics-based electrical model to experiments, we demonstrate that BTS cause reduced effective mobility and "slow" transistor turn-on with excessive gate voltage in monolayer 2D transistors, which sets a fundamental limit for their energy-efficient operation. We also show that BTS effects in 2D transistors could be mitigated with higher gate capacitance, with strain engineering, and by using bilayer instead of monolayer 2D channels, as long as $E_\rm U$ is reduced below ~ 50 meV. items.abstract: Optically exciting a typical low-dimensional semiconductor produces a nodeless \(s\)-type exciton as its lowest-energy bound state. Here, we explain how Coulomb phase matching stabilises a quantum-vortex exciton as the lowest bound state in flat Chern bands. We trace this behaviour to a gauge-invariant combination of exciton phase differences and Bloch-overlap phases that can reduce the Coulomb energy. items.title: Squeezed light from a semiconductor amplifier
items.abstract: The possibility of generating light in a squeezed quantum state during saturated light amplification in a semiconductor amplifier is theoretically analyzed. Due to four-wave mixing process during amplification, weak components of the spontaneous emission of the medium with symmetric frequency shifts relative to the strong amplified wave acquire the quantum properties of two-mode squeezed light. The squeezing of quadrature components occurs in the range of frequency shifts of several GHz ($\sim$ the inverse relaxation time of the charge carrier density) and can reach 10 dB or more under optimal conditions. The formation of a two-mode squeezing phase facilitates the observation of the squeezing effect, in which a strong wave, playing the role of a local wave, exhibits quadrature noise suppression without additional homodyne detection.

items.title: Hall conductance of dilute electrolytes from odd stochastic density functional theory
items.abstract: Electrolytes under an external magnetic field exhibit a Hall conductivity, much like metals and semiconductors. However, existing theories fail to quantitatively account for their measured Hall conductivities. To make progress toward such a theory, we develop a stochastic density functional framework for electrolytes in a magnetic field. This framework, which we dub odd SDFT, extends the celebrated stochastic density functional theory (SDFT) to incorporate transverse mobilities and chiral time-correlated noise. Using this framework, we calculate the Hall conductivity in the absence of hydrodynamic solvent effects through three approaches: (i) direct response, (ii) Green-Kubo relation, and (iii) a hybrid fluctuation-dissipation relation. We further show that odd SDFT applies more broadly to fluids with broken time-reversal and mirror symmetry, including odd-diffusive fluids and chiral act...

Vacancy aggregation enhances NV- spin coherence in diamond: a cluster-correlation-expansion study of multi-vacancy spin baths in semiconductors
items.abstract: Annealing a semiconductor makes its vacancies mobile; they aggregate into multi-vacancy complexes that often carry spin. Such centres are a magnetic-noise source for any spin qubit among them, in silicon and silicon carbide as well as in diamond, and they are accordingly blamed for NV-decoherence in irradiated and implanted diamond, with two coherence records credited to removing them. Cluster-correlation-expansion simulations driven by published electron-paramagnetic-resonance parameters invert that attribution. At a fixed paramagnetic spin density a multi-vacancy bath gives a Hahn-echo coherence time 3.1-7.1 times longer than a bath of isolated negative vacancies, over three decades of concentration. A bath dephases the qubit because its spins exchange spin projections with one another, and two can exchange only if their transition frequencies match. A fine-structure splitting shifts t...

Device contacts as spin-state selectors for silicon vacancies in 4H-SiC
items.abstract: Optically addressable defect spins in semiconductors are promising building blocks for scalable quantum technologies. Yet, the consequences of conventional contact schemes used in semiconductor device integration for the quantum spin environment remain largely unexplored. Using the silicon vacancy (V$_\mathrm{Si}$) in silicon carbide (SiC) as a model system, we show that a widely used contact metal, nickel (Ni), intrinsically perturbs the defect spin state and quenches the characteristic emission from the spin-quartet channel of V$_\mathrm{Si}$. Low-energy muon spin rotation further reveals that Ni contacts create a magnetically contaminated region extending at least $\sim$110 nm into the SiC, in stark contrast to non-magnetic contacts such as Ti and Al. Moreover, cross-sectional cathodoluminescence measurements on samples with high defect density demonstrate a suppressed quartet-state l...

items.title: An Emerging NVM-Based On-Chip Training Architecture with Non-Ideality Mitigation Through Bipolar Weight Distributions
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of deep learning has presented significant energy efficiency challenges to the conventional von Neumann architecture. In-memory computing (IMC) architectures based on emerging non-volatile memory (eNVM) are widely regarded as a promising solution for accelerating neural network training due to their high parallelism and low power consumption. However, the intrinsic non-idealities of eNVM devices can cause conductance updates to deviate from target values, thereby limiting the performance of on-chip training. To address this challenge, this paper presents a Non-ideality Optimized eNVM Accelerator (NOVA) architecture for on-chip training. Specifically, we first fabricate a two-dimensional (2D) ferroelectric field-effect transistor (FeFET) and develop a conductance modulation behavioral model calibrated with experimental data. Building upon this device model, we propos...

items.title: Optically Coupled Noise Spectroscopy Quantifies Defect Passivation in Monolayer MoS2 FETs
items.abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers are promising materials for electronic and photonic applications, yet the performance of chemical vapour deposition grown samples is severely limited by native sulphur vacancies that introduce mid-gap trap states, degrade carrier mobility, and elevate electrical noise. Here we investigate octanethiol passivation of sulphur vacancies in monolayer MoS2 field effect transistors, combining x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, photoluminescence, and Raman scattering with electrical transport and optically coupled low-frequency noise spectroscopy. Thiol treatment reduces the sulphur vacancy concentration from 7% to 4%, reducing the free electron density. Electrically, it increases the device resistance 35-fold while restoring gate switching with an on/off ratio of 10^4 and improving field-effect mobility from 1 to 5 cm^2/Vs. Low frequency noise spectrosc...

items.title: On-chip nanoplasma for adaptive electromagnetic protection
items.abstract: Over the past decade, semiconductor diodes have served as the primary switching elements in adaptive electromagnetic (EM) protection, yet their performance has been compromised by parasitic effects and thermal accumulation, rendering them inadequate against the rapidly evolving landscape of high-power microwave (HPM) threats. Here we show that on-chip nanoplasma switches (NPMS), composed of gallium nitride electrodes on silicon carbide substrates, exhibit superior radio frequency (RF) and thermal characteristics, positioning them as ideal field-driven switches in RF front-end protectors. By integrating NPMS into metasurfaces, antennas and circuit limiters, we achieve an adaptive response that ensures low-loss transmission for normal signals and high shielding against HPMs, while offering extended operating bandwidth and substantially higher tolerance than conventional solid-state devices...

items.title: Inverse-Designed High-Q/V Silicon Nitride Photonic Crystal Cavities for Second- and Third-Harmonic Generation
items.abstract: SiN photonic crystal (PhC) cavities are promising platforms for nonlinear and quantum photonics because of their wide transparency window, CMOS compatibility, and negligible two-photon absorption. However, realizing high-Q/V cavities remains challenging because of the relatively low refractive index of SiN. Here, we employ inverse design to optimize a two-dimensional SiN PhC cavity and experimentally demonstrate a quality factor of approximately 80,000, the highest reported for a near-stoichiometric SiN 2D PhC cavity. Furthermore, both second- and third-harmonic generation are observed from the same cavity, providing experimental evidence of strong optical confinement and large Q/V. Our results establish inverse-designed SiN PhC cavities as a promising platform for nonlinear photonics and future heterogeneous integrated photonic devices.

items.title: Approximate reservoir computing with a semiconductor laser for reducing energy consumption
items.abstract: Photonic reservoir computing is a promising physical machine-learning approach for time-series prediction. Quantization of the reservoir response signal is an important consideration in the implementation of photonic reservoir computing, and the number of quantization bits and sampling frequency need to be optimized to achieve high prediction performance and low energy consumption. However, few studies have investigated the effects of the number of quantization bits and sampling frequency on both prediction performance and energy consumption. In this study, we introduce the concept of approximate reservoir computing with a semiconductor laser by quantizing the reservoir node states and output weights. We numerically evaluate the performance of a chaotic time-series prediction task and estimate the energy consumption per sample using a component-level model. By optimizing the number of qu...

items.title: Photon-conserving Raman soliton attractors in focusing and defocusing Kerr media
items.abstract: The sign of the Kerr nonlinear coefficient has long been regarded as irrelevant to the direction of the Raman-induced soliton self-frequency shift. Yet the standard generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation (GNLSE) predicts a frequency shift that depends on the sign of the nonlinearity, which leads to an unphysical blue shift in the defocusing case. We resolve this inconsistency by deriving the time-domain form of the photon-conserving GNLSE (pcGNLSE) from its established frequency-domain counterpart. The derivation reveals that photon-number conservation imposes two sign modifications relative to the standard GNLSE: the Raman-shift coefficient acquires the absolute value of the Kerr nonlinear coefficient in place of its signed counterpart, and the self-steepening-Raman dissipation term likewise carries an absolute-value prefactor rather than a signed one. These two modifications jointl...

items.title: Graph-Based Kirchhoff Modeling of Non-Ohmic Electron Transport in Self-Assembled Nanonecklace Networks
items.abstract: Gold nanonecklace networks exhibit non-Ohmic current--voltage I-V characteristics with a sharp conduction threshold, making them promising for sensing and transistor-like devices. However, their conduction has been understood largely empirically, because experiments cannot see how conduction evolves inside the network. To address this, we develop a graph-based Kirchhoff modeling framework that resolves these internal processes, tracking the potential and current of every junction. Although every active element conducts linearly, the model reproduces the non-Ohmic response $I \propto (V-V_T)^ζ$. It also captures the experimentally observed effects of junction properties, network density, and voids, which lends confidence to its predicted internal states. These states show that the non-Ohmic response emerges from voltage-driven percolation. Conduction is governed by how junctions are conne...

items.title: Complex frequency-dependent quadrature squeezing in semiconductor lasers
items.abstract: We present a comprehensive study of quadrature squeezing in a quantum well laser based on a fully quantum Langevin approach. We compute the frequency-resolved squeezing map of the laser field and identify optimal squeezing curves, revealing, for the first time to our knowledge, both frequency-dependent squeezing and complex or hidden squeezing in a semiconductor laser. We further analyse the role of the linewidth enhancement factor (alpha-factor) in the emergence of these features. Our results establish semiconductor lasers as a platform for the generation of non-classical light and open new perspectives for their application in quantum communication and sensing.

items.title: Electron state tomography from quasiparticle interference maps
items.abstract: Characterizing electronic band structures requires precise knowledge of wave functions and their quantum geometry. Here, we introduce a tomography method to reconstruct the density matrix of electron states from quasiparticle interference maps around single impurities. We consider two-orbital models on a honeycomb lattice, relevant to graphene heterostructures and direct-gap semiconductors. For on-site impurities, backscattering between time-reversed states directly maps the density matrix populations and coherences into distinct orbital contributions in the interference map. While local probes usually lack orbital resolution, these orbital contributions transform under distinct symmetry group representations and can thus be disentangled to reveal the density matrix and quantum geometric tensor of the scattering states. This establishes impurities as tomographic probes for band structure...

items.title: Nanoscopic Multiplexing Optical Data Storage via Chip Fabrication
items.abstract: The accelerating growth of global data demands storage technologies combining high capacity, long lifetime and low energy consumption. Optical storage is attractive for archival applications, but conventional optical writing is constrained by diffraction-limited resolution and scalability, while thermal accumulation limits high-speed writing. Here we shift optical data writing from a serial optical process to a fabrication-defined process, in which lithographic masks govern where material modification occurs. Using patterned resist masks and ion implantation, we create fluorescent information voxels with nanoscale control over millimeter-scale areas. The platform supports multilevel and multidimensional encoding by independently encoding information in fluorescence intensity and wavelength. A machine-learning-assisted super-resolution reconstruction protocol is developed to recover infor...

items.title: Absorption and Phase-Contrast Microtomography Using Direct X-Ray Detection With Commercial Off-The-Shelf CMOS Sensors
items.abstract: This work presents high-resolution X-ray microtomography based on commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) CMOS image sensors as direct detectors. The system uses a microfocus X-ray source in cone-beam geometry, enabling both absorption-contrast imaging, thanks to the sensor s intrinsic resolution, and phase-contrast imaging, by adjusting the object-to-sensor distance. A dynamic flat-field correction algorithm mitigates radiation-induced sensor degradation during long acquisitions. The setup provides voxel sizes from 3.9 microns to 5.2 microns, with an effective spatial resolution (FWHM) as fine as 9.6 microns in magnified phase-contrast mode (1.33x) and 21 microns in non-magnified absorption-contrast mode. Phase contrast enhances visualization of soft tissue boundaries that are difficult to visualize using absorption-contrast imaging in the same experimental configuration.

items.title: Anharmonic Quantum Transport Analysis of Thermal Transport Anomalies in Ultrathin Silicon Nanowires
items.abstract: Thermal transport in low-dimensional semiconductors is important for nanoelectronics, quantum devices, and thermoelectrics. Recent molecular dynamics (MD) studies reveal a nonmonotonic diameter dependence of thermal conductivity in ultrathin silicon nanowires (NWs), but classical MD is limited at low temperatures and under strong confinement. Here, we investigate this anomaly using anharmonic non-equilibrium Green's function (NEGF) simulations combined with density functional theory-trained neuroevolution potentials. All transport results are expressed as effective thermal conductivities ($κ_{\mathrm{eff}}$) for NW devices with a finite channel length of $L=10$ nm. At 300 K, $κ_{\mathrm{eff}}$ decreases with diameter to minima at 6.24 and 5.50 nm for [001]- and [110]-oriented NWs, respectively. At 10 K, the corresponding minima occur at 7.33 and 5.50 nm. items.title: Predictive Software Scheduling as an Early-Warning Hint Layer for Optical Engine Thermal Drift in Heterogeneous SoIC Packaging
items.abstract: As semiconductor scaling approaches the A16 / 2 nm node, the integration of co-packaged optics (CPO) through TSMC's Compact Universal Photonic Engine (COUPE) architecture introduces critical thermal-optical coupling challenges. Micro-ring resonators embedded in the Photonic Integrated Circuit (PIC) layer are highly sensitive to temperature, with a wafer-level center wavelength deviation of merely +/-1.7 nm across a 300 mm wafer representing the platform's manufacturing control limit. To address this, we propose XRM-SSD V24, a physics-aware scheduling layer that models inference-load density 20-50 ms before execution and issues early-warning hints to the COUPE bias-control firmware, enabling pre-emptive thermal compensation. Simulation-based validation on a software emulation platform (physical characterization pending TSMC tape-out) over 90,000 inference steps yields a simulator-internal...

items.title: Speed Kills: Exploring Confused Deputy Attacks Through Edge AI Accelerators
items.abstract: AI Accelerators (AIAs) are specialized hardware, such as Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), that enable optimal and efficient execution of AI applications and on-device inference. The growing demand for AI applications has led to the widespread adoption of AIAs on edge and embedded devices. Unlike applications, AIAs are not bound by Operating System (OS) restrictions and have limited visibility into Application Processor (AP) security mechanisms (e.g., kernel versus application memory and process isolation). This semantic gap can lead to confused deputy vulnerabilities, where an AIA can be tricked by a malicious application into performing privileged operations on its behalf. In this paper, we conduct the first in-depth study of Confused Deputy Attacks (CDAs) using AIAs. We design DeputyHunt, a Large Language Model (LLM)-assisted framework to extract CDA-relevant information for a given AIA...

items.title: Energy Consumption in Next Generation Radio Access Networks
items.abstract: Historically, in macro-cell-based networks, the radio access network (RAN) portion accounts for the largest share of energy consumption in mobile networks. With greater densification, the transition to small cells and increased virtualization of the radio processing functions, the relative energy use of the different network segments is changing. At the same time, open radio access networks (O-RAN) have emerged as a promising approach to support this evolution through open interfaces that enable a multi-vendor environment, support for hierarchical intelligent controls, and simplified, cost-effective radio units that facilitate large-scale deployments. This paper examines the impact of these changes on energy consumption in next-generation RAN architectures through transaction-based energy models. Transaction-based network energy models were developed in 2009 to understand the evolution o...

items.title: Joint Architecture-Token-Bitwidth Multi-Axis Optimization of Vision Transformers for Semiconductor IC Packaging
items.abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) have achieved strong performance in visual recognition, yet their deployment in resource-constrained industrial environments remains limited. The main challenges are their high computational cost, memory requirements, and energy consumption. While individual efficiency techniques such as neural architecture search (NAS), token compression, and low-precision inference have been extensively studied, most prior work targets only a single optimization axis, limiting overall deployment gains while preserving accuracy. In this paper, we present one of the first holistic frameworks that jointly optimizes three complementary axes: architecture, token, and bit-width. Specifically, the framework identifies compact backbones via Neural Architecture Search (AutoFormer), reduces information processing via token merging (ToMe), and accelerates per-operation execution via fp1...
